status.headline: IEEPA additional duties have ended
status.summary: IEEPA additional ad valorem duties (the reciprocal action and the fentanyl/border actions) are no longer collected on covered entries on or after 2026-02-24 (EO 14389; CBP CSMS #67834313). They still appear in historical periods because they were lawfully in force and collected then.

refund_process.headline: A refund may be available for paid entries
refund_process.summary: Where IEEPA additional duties were paid, a refund may be available — the path depends on the entry's liquidation posture.
steps: Entry still unliquidated: file a Post-Summary Correction (PSC) to remove the IEEPA duty.
Entry liquidated within the last 180 days: file a protest under 19 U.S.C. 1514.
Otherwise: relief generally requires a timely, separately filed action — consult a customs attorney or licensed broker.
refund_process.caveat: Refunds are not automatic and are not guaranteed. Eligibility and amount depend on liquidation status, timeliness, and documentation.

litigation_risk.headline: Refund scope is subject to active litigation
litigation_risk.summary: The Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs. The government is challenging the scope of universal refund relief for certain finally liquidated entries, especially where the importer did not file its own CIT action.
litigation_risk.implication: Treat IEEPA refund recovery as probable-but-contingent for protected entries (unliquidated, timely protested, or covered by an importer's own CIT action), and as at-risk for finally liquidated entries with no individual action.
litigation_risk.source: Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariff authority; ongoing CIT / appellate proceedings

ui.flag_label: IEEPA duty ended — refund may apply
ui.flag_detail: SAIL applied the IEEPA additional duty for this period because it was in force then. Collection has since ended (2026-02-24). For entries on which IEEPA duty was paid, a refund may be available depending on liquidation status — not automatic, not guaranteed, and the scope of refund relief is being litigated.
ui.broker_diff: SAIL shows the IEEPA line for the period it was legally in force, using the statutory rate. If a broker did not bill IEEPA on a covered entry, that is consistent with an exemption or the post-2026-02-24 wind-down; if the broker did bill it, the duty may be recoverable via PSC or protest.
